builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: H-DDCM: Hadamard Codebooks for Fast Generative Image and Video Compression
summary: H-DDCM replaces the dense Gaussian codebooks of codebook-based training-free diffusion compression (e.g., Turbo-DDCM) with implicit randomized Hadamard dictionaries synthesized via the fast Walsh-Hadamard transform, and adds a table-free lexicographic scheme for combinatorial bitstream encoding. The cost is that encode/decode still runs full diffusion or flow-model inference per block, so end-to-end latency and quality remain bounded by the pretrained generator rather than by the codebook, and the method only pays off at ultra-low bitrates where perceptual, not distortion, metrics dominate. Adoption can fail if no suitable pretrained image/video diffusion model exists for the target domain, if rate-distortion (PSNR/SSIM) rather than perceptual quality is the requirement, or if the KV-cache re-encoding streaming scheme drifts on long videos.
rationale: The method targets a niche deployment case (generative compression at ultra-low bitrates) that presupposes access to a strong pretrained diffusion or flow generator, so it is worth tracking but not a default production adoption for a constrained-infrastructure team.
technique: Hadamard codebooks for training-free diffusion-based compression

The cost is that encode/decode still runs full diffusion or flow-model inference per block, so end-to-end latency and quality remain bounded by the pretrained generator rather than by the codebook, and the method only pays off at ultra-low bitrates where perceptual, not distortion, metrics dominate. Abstract claims O(d log d) compute and O(d) memory for dictionary projection versus materialized dense Gaussian codebooks, plus near-real-time streaming video compression on a single GPU; no numeric speedup or memory factor is reported in the abstract.
